_comment: Ground truth for the FIRST GENUINE PASSIVE ASSESSMENT (M9), step 10:
'compare the output against independently known vulnerabilities in the lab'.
Source of truth: OWASP Juice Shop is a deliberately vulnerable training application whose
weaknesses are published by its own project. The expectations below are limited to what a
PASSIVE scan can observe — response headers, cookie attributes, served content and transport.
They are NOT the Juice Shop challenge list: most of those challenges require active testing,
HOW TO USE THIS: after the live assessment completes, run
which reports expected-and-found, expected-and-missed (recall gaps) and found-but-unexpected
(candidates for review — they may be real, or they may be false positives worth a rule).
An expectation being missed is NOT automatically a defect: it may mean the crawl did not reach
the page, the budget was exhausted, or the deployment differs. The comparison report asks that

target.observable_by: passive observation only — no payloads, no active scanner

expectations.basis: Juice Shop ships no CSP by default; observable on any rendered page
default deployment sets no nosniff header
the lab serves plain HTTP; HSTS is absent and may validate as not_applicable
the lab target is HTTP-only and exposes a login form

expectations.expectation: Authentication token kept in browser storage
expectations.basis: Juice Shop stores its JWT client-side; observable in served JavaScript
X-Powered-By is commonly present on default Express apps
product and feedback APIs return createdAt/updatedAt

expectations.expectation: Cookie set without one or more of HttpOnly / SameSite
expectations.basis: Juice Shop sets a language/session cookie with minimal attributes

expectations.expectation: Forms served without an anti-CSRF token
expectations.basis: a SPA with token auth typically carries no CSRF token in forms
expectations.note: expected to validate as candidate: no passive rule can confirm a CSRF weakness

expectations.expectation: Third-party script loaded without Subresource Integrity
expectations.basis: depends on the build; recorded so its absence is noticed either way
Juice Shop's API surface; expected as attack-surface inventory, not as findings

not_expected_passively: SQL injection on the login form — requires payloads (active)
Reflected or stored XSS — requires payloads (active)
IDOR on basket or user objects — requires two accounts and crafted requests
Broken authentication / weak passwords — credential guessing is out of scope entirely
Business logic flaws (coupon, quantity, price) — no scanner confirms these
